Day 2 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
1228 AM CDT Thu Jul 30 2026

Valid 311200Z - 011200Z

...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS FROM IOWA
SOUTHWARD INTO THE OZARK PLATEAU...AND OVER THE CENTRAL AND SOUTHERN
HIGH PLAINS...

...SUMMARY...
At least isolated severe storms appear possible from Iowa southward
into the Ozark Plateau, and over the central and southern High
Plains Friday afternoon and evening. Sporadic occurrences of
damaging wind and large hail will be the primary hazards with a
conditional risk for a few tornadoes, mainly in Missouri.

...Synopsis...

A short-wave trough from the upper Midwest into mid MO Valley Friday
morning will translate into the mid MS Valley with a belt of 30-35
kt winds forecast within the western through southern periphery of
that feature. At the surface, an area of low pressure is expected to
undergo slight deepening while developing from northwest or central
IA at the start of the period into southern IL by late Friday night.
Meanwhile, a trailing cold front will advance south/southeast into
the southern Plains and Ozark Plateau.


...Lower Missouri and mid Mississippi Valleys into the Ozark
Plateau...

Mainly elevated showers and thunderstorms are expected to be ongoing
at 12Z Friday across portions of IA and MO within a zone of forcing
for ascent ahead of the mid-level system, and warm advection and
moisture transport along a 30-40 kt low-level jet. Those mechanisms
are likely to sustain deep convection through the morning into
afternoon east of the surface low, mainly across IL. In the wake of
the early-day storms and where cloud breaks can occur, daytime
heating combined with boundary-layer dewpoints in the low to mid 70s
is expected to yield a relatively narrow axis of moderate
instability with MLCAPE of 1000-2500+ J/kg.

Additional surface-based storms are expected to develop by early- to
mid afternoon initially near the surface low in south-central or
southeast IA with subsequent southward development along or ahead of
the front across MO. The 00Z CAMs suggest that the initial storm
mode will be semi-discrete, which is consistent with model forecasts
of 30-35 kt deep-layer shear vectors oriented largely perpendicular
to the initiating boundary. 

While some marginally severe hail is possible with any supercell
structures, warm mid-level temperatures will contribute to
considerable melting, potentially limiting that threat. Damaging
wind potential may be limited by storm mode with a more substantial
threat being dependent on upscale growth into clusters or a
cold-pool-driven MCS. Tornado potential remains unclear as the
models suggest the strongest low-level shear will remain displaced
to the east of the primary instability axis. That being said, a
conditional threat for a few tornadoes appears possible with: 1)
storms forming near or to the south of the surface low, should
modest low-level CAPE develop in the presence of locally enhanced
vertical vorticity, and 2) any supercells that can form in the warm
sector and move east into the stronger low-level shear forecast
across eastern MO during the late afternoon into evening. 

Given the above uncertainties, a level 1/Marginal Risk will be
maintained with this forecast.


...Colorado and New Mexico...

Initially northerly, post-frontal winds Friday morning are expected
to switch to northeast and then east by afternoon into evening,
supporting isolated to widely scattered thunderstorms along favored
terrain. MLCAPE on the order of 1000-2000 J/kg will coincide with
30-35 kt of deep-layer shear, suggesting the potential for at least
transient supercell structures capable of large hail. With time,
storms may grow upscale into clusters with a relatively deep,
well-mixed boundary layer enhancing the potential for locally severe
wind gusts. This is especially the case across parts of eastern NM
Friday evening where the merging of the terrain-induced storms and
cold-frontal storms could organize a more substantial cold pool.

..Mead.. 07/30/2026

Day 3 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0225 AM CDT Thu Jul 30 2026

Valid 011200Z - 021200Z

...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS PORTIONS
OF THE OHIO AND TENNESSEE VALLEYS INTO THE CENTRAL GULF COAST
STATES...AND OVER PARTS OF CENTRAL AND EASTERN NEW MEXICO...

...SUMMARY...
Isolated severe storms appear possible across portions of the Ohio
and Tennessee Valleys into the Central Gulf Coast states, and over
parts of central and eastern New Mexico Saturday afternoon and
evening.

...Synopsis...

A mid-level trough initially from the Great Lakes into the Ozark
Plateau Saturday morning is forecast to amplify over the lower OH
and the lower MS Valleys through Saturday night. In the low levels,
an area of low pressure is expected to develop from west-central IL
to the vicinity of the IN/KY border by 12Z Sunday. Meanwhile, a
trailing cold front will advance into the lower MS and the TN
Valleys.


...Ohio and Tennessee Valleys into the central Gulf Coast states...

A fairly widespread area of showers and thunderstorms is expected to
be ongoing at 12Z Saturday across portions of the lower OH, TN, and
lower MS Valleys. A subset of that convection is likely to persist
into afternoon within the pre-frontal warm sector, aided by height
falls aloft, warm advection, and moisture transport along a 25-35 kt
low-level jet (LLJ). On the western flank of the more persistent
storms, cloud breaks may allow for stronger heating of a moist
boundary layer, yielding a potentially narrow axis of moderate
instability by afternoon ahead of the cold front. 

Diurnally enhanced storms appear likely within the corridor of
greater air mass destabilization, generally from central KY and
middle TN into MS, AL, and potentially western GA. While the
strongest deep-layer shear is forecast across the northern edge of
the warm sector, mainly north of the OH River, an area of stronger
low-level shear may persist across portions of KY and TN, coincident
with the southern extension of the LLJ. Locally damaging wind gusts
appear to be the primary hazard with the most intense storms;
however, some tornado threat could materialize from portions of IN
and OH into middle TN within the zone of stronger low-level shear.


...Central and eastern New Mexico...

There is some model signal for a weak mid-level disturbance to
progress south within the eastern periphery of the upper high on
Saturday. The glancing influence of that feature will combine with
the upslope flow of a moist and moderately unstable air mass to
generate afternoon thunderstorms along the favored terrain. While
vertical shear is not expected to be particularly strong, the
presence of steep low/mid-level lapse rates may support a few severe
storms capable of large hail and damaging winds.

..Mead.. 07/30/2026

$$

Day 4-8 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0335 AM CDT Thu Jul 30 2026

Valid 021200Z - 071200Z

...DISCUSSION...
...Days 4 and 5/Sunday and Monday...

The models remain in relatively good agreement in depicting a strong
short-wave trough and attending belt of mid-level flow progressing
along the international border from the northern Rockies into the
northern Plains. Meanwhile, an associated cold front is forecast to
move into the northern High Plains on Sunday and the upper MS Valley
into northern Plains on Monday. Low-level ridging from the Great
Lakes into Ozark Plateau may disrupt the advection of a maritime
tropical air mass ahead of the front. However, evapotranspiration
will contribute to pockets of higher moisture content, which,
combined with the eastern extension of an EML plume, will contribute
to moderate instability ahead of a surface cold front both
afternoons.

On Sunday, the strongest forcing for ascent associated with a lead 
vorticity lobe is expected to remain across SK and MB with capping
to the south of that feature potentially limiting storm coverage
along the front in ND. On the condition that storms develop, the
presence of moderate instability and 30-40 kt of deep-layer shear
would support storm organization and at least an isolated severe
weather threat. Additional severe storms appear possible from the
Mid-Atlantic into Southeast ahead of a short-wave trough moving
through the Great Lakes, OH Valley, and Gulf Coast states.  

On Monday, a secondary disturbance and associated jet streak are
forecast to move into the northern Plains, supporting a potentially
greater severe weather threat from the northern Plains into the
upper MS Valley. 


...Days 6 through 8/Tuesday through Thursday...

The 00Z deterministic and ensemble mean solutions indicate
low-amplitude troughing across the north-central states on Tuesday
with a belt of enhanced mid-level flow extending from the northern
Rockies into the upper Great Lakes. A few severe storms appear
possible over the central High Plains where the southern periphery
of the stronger mid-level flow is juxtaposed with a moist and
unstable upslope regime. 

By Wednesday and Thursday, the ensemble mean solutions indicate a
modestly enhanced belt of quasi-zonal flow across the northern tier
of the CONUS. However, there is considerable spread across the
deterministic models with the location and track of disturbances
embedded within that air stream. As such, confidence in the location
and extent of any severe weather threat is low.

..Mead.. 07/30/2026

Day 1 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
1121 AM CDT Thu Jul 30 2026

Valid 301630Z - 311200Z

...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS PORTIONS OF
SOUTH DAKOTA...NEBRASKA...AND NORTH-CENTRAL KANSAS...

...SUMMARY...
Thunderstorms with severe wind gusts and isolated large hail will be
possible this afternoon and evening across parts of the central and
northern Plains, but especially across parts of South Dakota,
Nebraska, and north-central Kansas. Isolated severe wind gusts may
also occur across parts of the Southeast.

...Northern/Central Plains...
Showers and thunderstorms are currently ongoing within a modest
warm-air advection regime from central SD into northeast NE. These
storms will likely weaken over the next few hours as the low to
mid-level flow decreases. This should allow for sufficient airmass
recovery/destabilization by the late afternoon across much of the
region. Recent surface analysis depicted 70s dewpoints into far
south-central NE, as well as pockets of greater low-level moisture
in western SD and ahead of a cold front in northeast ND. Heating
within this moist environment to the west of the ongoing storms (and
associated cloudiness) is expected to result in a corridor of strong
to very strong buoyancy by this afternoon. 

Current satellite imagery shows a shortwave trough moving across
southeast MT and WY. Expectation is for this wave to continue
eastward, interacting with the destabilized and buoyant airmass
across the north/central Plains to support thunderstorm development.
Initial development appears most likely across western/central SD
where the ascent attendant to this shortwave trough will be
augmented by mesoscale lift near a surface low currently over
southwest SD. A more cellular mode is likely early in the convective
cycle, with a trend towards a more clustered/linear mode thereafter.
Primary threat will be strong gusts with some isolated hail
possible, particularly early during the more cellular mode. 

In addition to the low over southwest SD, recent surface analysis
placed another low over northwest KS. Weak troughing between these
lows, likely sharpened by baroclinicity driven by differential
heating, could act as a favorable corridor for forward propagation
if a more coherent linear structure materializes.

...Eastern ND into northern MN...
Thunderstorm development is expected this afternoon from eastern ND
into northern MN along a southeastward-progressing cold front
forecast to move through the region. Moderate buoyancy will precede
this front, but vertical shear will be modest, limiting storm
organization and duration. Even so, buoyancy will be strong enough
for occasional damaging gusts and isolated instances of hail.

...Northern/Central High Plains...
Pockets of moderate instability may develop in parts of eastern
Colorado, western Kansas and eastern Montana. Although large-scale
ascent will be weak in these areas, topographic forcing will aid
convective initiation. During the mid/late afternoon into evening,
isolated to scattered storms will move east-southeastward into the
lower elevations, with localized strong to severe wind gusts and
hail possible. Slightly stronger vertical shear is possible across
north-central/northeast MT, where a few more organized storms are
possible.

...Central Gulf Coast into northern FL/southern GA...
A modest baroclinic boundary extends from central AL southeastward
through southern/southeast GA. Dewpoints to the south of this
boundary are in the 70s, with temperatures already in the upper
80s/low 90s. Moderate to strong buoyancy will continue to build
across this region south of the boundary, with low-level convergence
contributing to scattered to widespread thunderstorm development.
Vertical shear will remain weak, and a largely disorganized
multicellular storm mode is expected. Even so, water loading within
some of the stronger storms that develop and mature could result in
isolated damaging wind gusts through late afternoon/early evening.

..Mosier/Moore.. 07/30/2026
